properties.areaDesc: Davis Mountains; Davis Mountains Foothills
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 7:14PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 714 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 8
miles southeast of Kent. This thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of southwestern
Reeves, north central Jeff Davis and southeastern Culberson Counties.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 10 between mile markers 178 and 194.
Interstate 20 between mile markers 0 and 5.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT SOUTHWESTERN REEVES...NORTH CENTRAL JEFF DAVIS AND SOUTHEASTERN CULBERSON COUNTIES THROUGH 800 PM CDT

properties.areaDesc: Coastal New Hanover; Coastal Georgetown
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 27 at 8:11PM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Coastal New Hanover County. In
South Carolina, Coastal Georgetown County.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT Wednesday through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 27 at 3:36PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

No flooding is expected at this time, however residents living near
local rivers and streams should be vigilant of the potential for ice
in culverts and other stream passage structures to restrict flow
resulting water flowing over roads in affected areas.

and Conejos River.

Southeastern Rio Grande County, and Southwestern Alamosa County...

especially in low-lying areas.

agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying areas.

counties are impacted, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.

properties.areaDesc: Chaves, NM; Lincoln, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 27 at 5:25PM MDT until October 27 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 525 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln and Western Chaves
Counties.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

Both localized and distant heavy rainfall will create sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 2:56PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest
tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels
expected during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and perhaps nuisance
flooding of low-lying areas will be possible with each upcoming
high tide due to the persistent onshore winds. Maximum water
levels will reach between 1 and 2 ft above the normal highest
tide line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. A
brief break in winds and elevated water levels is forecast late
Wednesday, but a second round of elevated water levels and
persistent southerly winds are forecast with the arrival of yet
another front late Thursday into Friday.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.
